intro: The research board for /uk-locations/blue-staffy-puppies-manchester-uk/: https://claude.ai/artifact/WydQDtbxSc4WdJ5mfFEhkN. Nothing is outlined until you pick. Claude's recommendation is marked on each question.

questions.context: Recommended: (a) M1, colour comes last. Why: none of Google's top five puts "blue" in its title or H1, and the planner has the general Staffy phrases at 100–1K a month against 10–100 for every blue phrase. "Breed and health first, colour second" serves both, opens on the top-scored question ("are the parents health-tested", score 6), and agrees with Manchester's ChatGPT answer and the Kennel Club breed page, which put health and temperament over colour. Our prices go by sex, never by coat (data/price-matrix.json). Trade-off: the H1 does not carry the deposit fear or the delivery warning, so the second section must answer both; and a breeder named for the colour is saying colour comes last.

options.label: M1: "Should Colour Decide Which Blue Staffy Puppy Comes Home to Manchester?" (breed, health and the parents first; colour last; prices that never move with coat)
M2: "Is It Safe to Have a Blue Staffy Puppy Delivered to Manchester?" (seen on video before it travels; puts the deposit-scam fear in the H1, but argues with ChatGPT's "don't have it delivered")
M3: "Who Will You Call Once Your Blue Staffy Puppy Is Settled in Manchester?" (after the advert ends: support, the guarantee, take-back; the weakest search fit)

questions.context: Recommended: (a) S2. Why: the prose lane is empty. The question file treats 7 of 8 page-one pages as listings, and the eighth (Freeads) is a 45-advert feed. Most of their "Manchester" pages list dogs from outside Greater Manchester (Pets4Homes 9 of 24 cards, puppies.co.uk 0 of 3). A signed breeder page answers the buyer they leave unanswered. Blue stays in the H1 (the page's own H1 and URL), while the title carries the for-sale family the strategy row scores 10, high. Trade-off: it gives up Google's page-one H1 shape (every result says "for sale", none says blue), boroughs get one line each inside the delivery answer, and it is the most writing of the three.

options.label: S2: blue in the H1, "for sale" in the title; one named breeder answering the Greater Manchester buyer; boroughs named in the delivery answer
S1: Strategy A's Manchester row as written (the full-breed for-sale phrase, no colour, led by ChatGPT's checklist)
S3: staffy puppies for sale across Greater Manchester (the for-sale family leads title and H1, the litter as a priced table, the boroughs as their own section group)

questions.question: Which strategy direction?

questions.context: Recommended: (a). - Hero and opening: EEBP (who sells, where the puppies are, prices and delivery in the first sentence) - The deposit and viewing: PDB (the reader arrives with a named fear) - The litter and prices: FAB (each inclusion turned into a benefit; never explained by coat colour) - Delivery to Greater Manchester: FAB (collection weighed against delivery, honestly) - Health and raising: EEBP (microchip and vaccinations, ChatGPT's two high-band checks, on the vet-signed health card) - Life in Manchester: QAB (four of the six People Also Ask questions are life questions) - The FAQ blocks: QAB - Contact: AIDA (the action stage, from data) Header style: Style 2, conversational hybrid in the FAQ register (each header a buyer question that also carries a keyword; London's outline rewrote 8 headings at STOP 2 to add one).

Recommended: (a). Why: the page's H1 and URL already say blue, and S2 puts the for-sale family in the title and first 100 words, so the page answers both searches. Volumes are planner ranges where Google returned the phrase; the rest name why no figure was read. Recommended: (a). Trade-off: placements are proposals; the outline (STOP 2) settles each one.

questions.context: The rebuilt question file picked "Are both parents DNA tested clear for L-2-HGA and HC-HSF4?" for the middle FAQ. We name the tests and share certificates on request, but no result is on file, so the page cannot answer "clear". The question builder should have blocked it. Recommended: (a). Trade-off: none; (b) keeps a question whose honest answer reads as evasive.

questions.context: The default limits were never measured. Measured against 17 competitor pages (15 are listing grids) and London as built, no fixed set holds up: the counts point both ways, and the page gate and the board's density table count the same page differently, by up to about 20 times. The full report: docs/reports/ki99-location-calibration-2026-10-07.md. Recommended: (a). Trade-off: it is a small gate change with its own tests, and the "blue staffy" limit is tight, so Manchester's outline must plan under it.

options.label: Limits that scale with the page's length, on the board's own counter (London fits under every one, so its special entry can go)
New fixed numbers (London fails "blue staffy"; the city limit would never bite; the two tools still disagree)
Keep the defaults and give each city its own limits from its approved board
